newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Crown Cork in Colombian joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Crown Cork in Colombian joint venture.

text.p: Colombia's Ardila Lulle industrial conglomerate unveiled plans Monday for a joint venture with U.S. packaging company Crown Cork & Seal Co Inc to set up a $40 million canned drinks plant.

The factory, to be operated by the newly-formed company known as Crown Colombiana SA, would be built in Tocancipa, about 60 miles (100 km) north of Bogota, and is expected to begin operations by the end of this year.

Carlos Alberto Beltran, chairman of soda-manufacturer Gaseosas Postobon -- flagship of the Ardila Lulle group -- said the plant would include a two piece can manufacturing line and would have a production capacity of 600 million cans per year in the initial phase.

"We will be canning beer, sodas, malted beverages and other soft drinks. We hope this will enable us to expand our market share in the canned drinks market. We are also thinking about exporting," Beltran told Reuters.
He said the plant's output could be doubled as market conditions dictated.

Ardila Lulle is one of the major players in the Colombian drinks market. It currently produces 572 million gallons (22 million hectoliters) of beer and soft drinks per year and is in heavy competition with the Santo Domingo industrial conglomerate, which includes brewing giant Bavaria SA.
The Ardila Lulle group currently imports most of its cans from Panama, Puerto Rico and Mexico.
